description: A scrap of paper wedged into a crack in the wall, right where someone landing here would see it.
A crumpled scrap of paper.  Whoever wrote it was in a hurry, or in the dark.
A note folded small and held tight.  The edges are stained brown.
A page torn from a parking security logbook.  Neat handwriting at the top, less neat at the bottom.

//: Left in arrival alcoves. Each hints at one or two things, never everything. Some are wrong or cut off on purpose.

text.text: Lights are worth more than food.  Don't let yours die.
Boil it.  All of it.  Even if it looks clean.
Follow the marker arrows.  Not the signs.
If something is grinning at you, you're already standing in the dark.
The stairwells go up.  Keep trying.
Day 3.  Found people.  They have a room with a door and a kettle.  Look for the word BREAKROOM.
Don't sleep where the lights are out.  Don't sleep where the lights are on either, if you're alone.
The wall you came through still works.  It just won't take you home.
Count the pillars.  Write it down.  It won't help, but write it down.
if you hear running on all fours, stand still and make yourself big.  they don't like a fight.  they
The moths aren't after you.  They're after your torch.  Same thing, in the end.
WELCOME TO LEVEL 1.  Somebody crossed out WELCOME.

//: Scattered through Level 1: lockers, wrecks, camp stores. Bits of other people's stories.

text.text: Car's out of gas on what the sign called P4.  I've walked down eleven ramps since then.  There is no P5.  There is no P4 either.
Traded my good boots for two bottles at the sandbag camp.  Worth it.  Don't tell Dot.
Marcus says the map is wrong because the place moves.  I think the map is wrong because Marcus can't draw.
Third night without the light in bay C.  Whatever lives in the dark there has learned my name.  It doesn't say it right.
Note to self: the vending machines take the grey cards.  Find more grey cards.
Jenna went to check the noise by the elevators.  The elevators don't open.  Jenna didn't come back.
There's a generator in a side room off the east lane.  Two cans of gas and the lights come on for a week.  A WEEK.
Saw someone I knew from before.  Walked right up to them.  It wasn't them.
Don't go where the lights are all out.  Or go, but bring three flashlights and leave before they die.
The water tastes of pennies.  The almond water tastes of nothing at all.  I've started dreaming about it.
If you find this, the cage key is NOT under the mat.  I checked.  Sorry.
The lobby lifts run.  Press the button once.  Don't watch the walls on the way.  When the doors open somewhere dark, walk.  Don't wait for them to open again.  They won't.
Dot says the lobbies are the only rooms the grinning things leave alone.  Not the moths, though.  We're setting up in the one past the blue van.  Bring tea.

//: Found on the dead at overrun camps.

text.text: They came when the brazier went out.  We had fuel.  Nobody wanted to be the one to get up.
Tell the Breakroom we tried.  Tell them the sandbags were never the problem.
Lost two to the dark and one to the water.  Going to try the walls again tomorrow.  If there is a tomorrow, this note is useless.
I'm writing this so someone knows we were here.  We were here.  Five of us.  We were here.
0200 rounds complete.  Camera 4 showing a smile.  Not a face.  Just the smile.  Reported to nobody, because there is nobody.
No date.  Monitors are static except camera 4.  Camera 4 shows the room I'm in.  I'm not in the picture.
Shift log: lights failing in sectors C through F.  Generator in maintenance B still good.  Fuel low.  Moths bad near the good lights.
Incident: unknown person in grey coat tried the door.  Asked for water.  Didn't have a face under the hood.  Did not open the door.

//: Spray paint on the concrete by earlier travellers. Some help, some don't.
text: THEY ONLY COME IN THE DARK
